planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Red Volunteer bears clear candle-red self flowers with a contrasting golden-yellow throat on tall, well-branched scapes.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Bred by Oakes and introduced in 1984, Red Volunteer bears large, 7-inch, clear candle-red flowers with a contrasting golden-yellow throat on well-branched scapes about 30 inches tall. This dormant tetraploid opens a heavy, prolific flush of blooms over many weeks in midsummer and has gone on to become a widely used hybridizing parent with dozens of registered offspring. It has received American Hemerocallis Society honors including the Honorable Mention and Award of Merit. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Stafford Daylily (RHS Award of Garden Merit Red Self)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Stafford bears narrow-petaled, deep velvety red flowers with a yellow throat and benefits from light afternoon shade in the hottest climates to prevent sun-scorch.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, though a little light afternoon shade helps protect the bright scarlet-red blooms from sun-scorch in very hot climates. Bred by Randall and introduced in 1959, Stafford bears narrow-petaled, deep bright velvety red flowers about four inches across with a yellow throat, held on scapes to roughly 28 inches tall. It flowers later in the season, from June into August, and has earned the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for its reliable garden performance and relative resistance to hemerocallis gall midge. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigorous bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Apricot Symphony bears large peach-pink blend flowers above a gold-peach throat on tall, vigorous scapes.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun. Bred by Roy Klehm and registered in 2003, Apricot Symphony bears large, 6.5-inch peach-pink blend flowers above a gold-peach throat, carried on scapes about 32 inches tall. It blooms in an early-to-midseason flush and forms a vigorous, floriferous clump over time. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain heavy flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Apricot Sparkles forms a compact clump of diamond-dusted apricot flowers with ruffled petal edges and reblooms readily.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun. A patented selection from Dr. Darrell Apps' breeding program introduced by Pat Stamile, Apricot Sparkles is a compact diploid bearing apricot, diamond-dusted flowers with ruffled petal margins and smooth sepals on scapes only about 15 inches tall. It is an unusually early and prolific bloomer, opening its first flush in late May to early June and following with a strong second flush of rebloom later in the season. Its small stature suits edging and front-of-border placement. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Frosted Amethyst bears fragrant lavender-blue self flowers above a green throat on compact scapes.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun. Bred by Jack Carpenter and registered in 1992, Frosted Amethyst is a fragrant, semi-evergreen diploid bearing lavender-blue self flowers about five inches across above a clean green throat, held on scapes roughly 20 inches tall. It blooms in a midseason-to-late flush and forms a tidy, floriferous clump. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Warrior Victorious bears fragrant purple flowers patterned with a lavender-blue watermark above a green throat and reblooms reliably.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun. Bred by Jack Carpenter and registered in 2007 from a cross of Essence of Royalty and Texas Blue Eyes, Warrior Victorious is a fragrant, semi-evergreen tetraploid bearing purple flowers about 5.5 inches across patterned with a lavender-blue watermark above a green throat, held on scapes around 26 inches tall. It opens an early-to-midseason flush and reblooms reliably through summer. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Fancy Face Daylily (Cream-Gold with Mahogany Eyezone)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Fancy Face bears fragrant cream-gold flowers patterned with a dark mahogany eyezone above a green throat and reblooms over summer.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun. Bred by Jack Carpenter and registered in 1994, Fancy Face is a fragrant, evergreen diploid bearing cream-gold flowers about 5.5 inches across patterned with a dark mahogany eyezone above a green throat, held on scapes around 22 inches tall. It opens an early-to-midseason flush and reblooms over the summer. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.
